newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - May 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - May 5.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Renegade Moro Islamic Liberation Front rebels have demanded ransom of 25 million pesos for a Chinese businessman abducted on Friday and 15 million pesos for a Philippine Airline executive abducted late last month, Army authorities said. (MALAYA)

- The government blamed China yesterday for the latest tension in bilateral relations, which was fuelled by the recent incursion of three Chinese naval vessels in the disputed Spratlys in the South China Sea. (STAR)
- The Office of the Ombudsman has cleared former Agriculture Secretary Roberto Secretary Roberto Sebastian of charges in connection with the rice shortage that hit the country in 1995. (INQUIRER)
- The Philippine Central Bank will tighten screening procedures for top officials of commercial and thrift banks to prevent another debacle similar to Monte Piedad and Savings Bank. (INQUIRER)

- The Senate must come out with its own version of the last component of the Comprehensive Tax Reform Programme before the end of the month to beat the deadline set for the country's historic exit from the International Monetary Fund. (STAR)

- Credit expansion has slowed down during the first two months of the year, an indication that commercial banks' lending activities have begun to stabilise, according to the Philippine Central Bank. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
